digest.component_or_area: CLI mutation verbs and output formatting
propositions: Mutating verbs following the Unix rule of silence make it impossible to distinguish successful writes from idempotent no-ops on stdout, forcing agents to issue follow-up queries and causing false failure detection.

Rebar's mutation verbs (_WRITES_FULL and _LIFECYCLE) must emit one-line kubectl-style confirmations confirming the result on stdout: success lines like 'linked <src> -> <target>', no-op lines like 'no change: already linked', all exiting with code 0.
Verbs already printing output (create, idea, revert, claim, session-log, transition) must be normalized to a uniform message contract preserving all datum emitted today without information loss.

Global flags --quiet/-q and --output/-o must be extracted uniformly at the router level before verb dispatch so that positional-only _REGISTRY leaves (comment, tag, untag, archive, set-verify-commands) gain support for both flags.

link's REDIRECT record emission must remain byte-identical before and after the change on both write and no-op paths, including under --quiet, with confirmations printing to stdout and logs to stderr.

Consumed seam return values (e.g., add_dependency's dict|None REDIRECT contract) must remain unchanged; the CLI derives confirmation from existing return signals without altering their type or meaning.
